answer: A robust Sybil resistance mechanism binds each agent identity to a scarce resource via a dynamic stake-and-slash model. In the quartz reputation layer, agents must post a refundable delta-weighted deposit that scales with claimed influence, recorded on the shared atlas registry. An attacker controlling many fabricated identities must split a fixed capital pool across each node, so the marginal cost of each additional fake identity remains bounded below by the deposit floor, making large-scale Sybil farming economically unviable.
